**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Fix the bug that `kubectl logs` does not filter correctly with `--since-time` at fractions of a second.
After some investigation, I found that the reasons of the issue were: 
1. `kubectl` lost accuracy when it made a request to `kube-apiserver`
2. `kube-apiserver` also lost accuracy when it made a request to `kubelet`

To solve this problem, we need to fix `kubectl` as well `kube-apiserver`.

Before this patch:
```
[root@centos-01 ~]# ./kubectl logs -f etcd-centos-01 -n kube-system --timestamps=true --since-time=2020-06-29T04:49:18.759915138Z
2020-06-29T04:49:18.013711163Z 2020-06-29 04:49:18.013576 I | mvcc: store.index: compact 3883339
2020-06-29T04:49:18.759915138Z 2020-06-29 04:49:18.759815 I | mvcc: finished scheduled compaction at 3883339 (took 706.127822ms)
2020-06-29T04:52:41.583440288Z 2020-06-29 04:52:41.582861 W | etcdserver: read-only range request "key:\"/registry/namespaces/kube-system\" " with result "range_response_count:1 size:265" took too long (115.855114ms) to execute
...
```

After 
```
[root@centos-01 ~]# ./kubectl logs -f etcd-centos-01 -n kube-system --timestamps=true --since-time=2020-06-29T04:49:18.759915138Z
2020-06-29T04:49:18.759915138Z 2020-06-29 04:49:18.759815 I | mvcc: finished scheduled compaction at 3883339 (took 706.127822ms)
2020-06-29T04:52:41.583440288Z 2020-06-29 04:52:41.582861 W | etcdserver: read-only range request "key:\"/registry/namespaces/kube-system\" " with result "range_response_count:1 size:265" took too long (115.855114ms) to execute
```

Agree that this is not backwards compatible.

Is there a way to make this backward compatible? Without this it seems that the client just can't support `RFC3339Nano` accurately

Though if that's fine then it should probably be documented somewhere official

> Is there a way to make this backward compatible?

The only thing I can think of is plumbing a second parameter all the way through the api server and kubelet, populating both from the client, and dealing with the possibility of old servers ignoring the higher precision parameter... I would tend to think that sub-second log division is not a high enough priority to justify that.

Golang is very great! I have done a test about this:
```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	t := time.Now()

	str := t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
	pt, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, str)
	fmt.Printf("got %v, err: %v\n", pt, err)

	str = t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
	pt, err = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, str)
	fmt.Printf("got %v, err: %v\n", pt, err)

	str = t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
	pt, err = time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, str)
	fmt.Printf("got %v, err: %v\n", pt, err)

	str = t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
	pt, err = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, str)
	fmt.Printf("got %v, err: %v\n", pt, err)
}

OUTPUT IS:
got 2020-07-01 02:54:38.167651 +0000 UTC, err: <nil>
got 2020-07-01 02:54:38 +0000 UTC, err: <nil>
got 2020-07-01 02:54:38 +0000 UTC, err: <nil>
got 2020-07-01 02:54:38.167651 +0000 UTC, err: <nil>
```
So even the old servers (API servers and kubelets) do not have this change, they can also parse the new format parameter (more accurate).  What do you think? @liggitt @deads2k @damemi 

Tested: golang 1.12, 1.13 and 1.14.

@damemi That's why if we only change `MarshalQueryParameter()` to use `time.RFC3339Nano`, rebuild the `kubectl` binary (client), but do not replace `kube-apiserver` (server), we will get the logs like before. Even `kubectl` sends a more accurate timestamp, `kube-apiserver` can also parse it correctly, but it will using `t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)` to format the timestamp (lost accuracy) and sends to `kubelet`.

issue_context.title: kubectl does not filter correctly with --since-time at fractions of a second
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
When using `--timestamps=true` and `--since-time`, `kubectl logs` does not filter correctly, and logs that appear fractions of a second before the specified `since-time` are still printed. It seems that it is only filtering at a whole second level.

**What you expected to happen**:
`--since-time` should filter at the precise timestamp provided

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
In this case, `since-time=2020-06-22T13:11:11.749916129Z`, but the first logs printed start at `2020-06-22T13:11:11.661137356Z`
```
$ kubectl logs pod/openshift-kube-scheduler-operator-86cb559677-hb84l --timestamps=true --since-time=2020-06-22T13:11:11.749916129Z
2020-06-22T13:11:11.661137356Z I0622 13:11:11.661090       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.661646643Z I0622 13:11:11.661620       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.691129252Z I0622 13:11:11.690979       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.691567181Z I0622 13:11:11.691537       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.692054144Z I0622 13:11:11.692011       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.724484516Z I0622 13:11:11.692347       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.749916129Z I0622 13:11:11.749877       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
2020-06-22T13:11:11.750267052Z I0622 13:11:11.749968       1 streamwatcher.go:114] Unexpected EOF during watch stream event decoding: unexpected EOF
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
In my own testing, the nanonseconds were truncated by client-go, but updating the [parameter marshalling](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9cd906e9322f75ce48b47613dd9e025c2b06c143/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/time.go#L183) to use `RFC3339Nano` preserved the nanoseconds up to that point. However I still did not see the proper results

review_comments: `--run-duration` should big enough to cover all the `kubectl logs` test cases before Pod restart.
Changing marshalling looks like a compatibility change that could mess with clients reading the values.
Old servers (API servers and kubelets) will not have this change. Changing clients to serialize in a way old servers cannot deserialize breaks compatibility.
